notes: This face is predominantly handwritten formula and drawing work on a reused sheet/envelope carrying a sideways typed address. The address, the separated typed 5, and archive digit 2 are the only readable nonmathematical textual material on this face.

No additional typed passage beyond the address is genuinely legible. Pale traces behind the main ink include recognizable mathematical-looking handwritten fragments and indistinct shapes, but they do not yield a securely readable typed line on this face. No wording has been reconstructed from H's editorial mention of show-through.

The page presents F-data, s/t and sigma arrows, mu symbols, a/l/r, a short map, products of triangular symbols, and lower formulas involving Ob and Fl. These are observational descriptions; no categorical identification or theorem is claimed.

No manuscript date, title, or own folio is visible. The handwritten 2 at lower left is treated only as an archive sheet number. The typed 5 belongs to the address label and is not promoted to a manuscript folio.
No explicit author doubt such as a question mark or verbal hesitation is present. Reader uncertainty marks concern damaged, overwritten, very small or clipped ink, not authorial doubt.

The final line has no readable subscript on its initial F, one visible relation bar, two primes on the last n, and a closing parenthesis without a visible corresponding opening one. It is preserved as supplied, without mathematical repair.

The drawings are checked approximations in TikZ. Distinct gaps, returns, dots, points, arrows, hatches and doubled strokes were considered; pressure texture and paper grain are not separately encoded.
Both C and H were checked where they agreed: this revealed a doubled F in the second Fl of the last line and the omitted separate lower-right oblique rule.
Only this scan and the authorized packet, preamble, and notation snapshot were read. No OCR, web source, other scan, other reader output, or published parallel text was used.
